title: one possible man-camp cabin 004 - Fisher Place - Arnegard North Dakota - 2013-07-03
description:
Inside a man-camp:  Looking at a sample room in a mobile home set up as a man-camp.

Man-camps can house anywhere from 200 to 2,500 people.  Most are around 500 to 1,500 beds.  Oil workers, nearly all of them single men in their 20s and 30s, are the target resident.  Man-camps can take several forms:

• Some are endless small plots of concrete, on which a teardrop camper is placed.  Each trailer is hooked up to water, sewer, and electricity.
• Some are mobile homes, with small 12 x 15 foot rooms with little more than a shower bathroom, tiny desk, coffee pot, and small closet.  Each room is hooked up to water, sewer, and electricity.
• Some are manufactured homes, with small 12 x 15 foot rooms with little more than a shower bathroom, tiny desk, coffee pot, and small closet.  Each room is hooked up to water, sewer, and electricity.
• Some are a series of manufactured cabins, with small 12 x 15 foot rooms with little more than a shower bathroom, tiny desk, coffee pot, and small closet.  Each cabin is hooked up to water, sewer, and electricity.  Larger cabins sleep two per room, but most are singles. However, the cabins are almost always duplexes.
• Some are single-story dormitories, with small 12 x 15 foot rooms with little more than a tiny desk, coffee pot, and small closet.  Some dormitories have shower bathroom in each room, but some have large, shared showers and toilets at one end.  Each dormitory offers water, sewer, and electricity.

Some man-camps provide a "dining hall" where a buffet meal is served for breakfast and dinner.  Some also provide an "entertainment hall" with several big-screen TVs, many video game terminals, many DVD and blu-ray players, etc.  But some provide slightly more cooking ability in the room (via a microwave, hot plate, or kitchenette), and do not provide communal dining.  A large number provide no entertainment whatsoever.

Increasingly, public drunkenness and drunk driving are encouraging counties in North Dakota to strictly regulate man-camps.  Man-camps, in turn, are providing more on-site services for the residents, such as entertainment halls.  This keeps residents on-site, instead of driving around drunk or getting into trouble.

Generally speaking, a single room like this at a man-camp can go for $1,200 to $1,500 a month.  More expensive man camps can run $1,700 a month.  (Single-family two-bedroom homes in the area can go for $2,500 a month or more.)

At the Fisher Place farm (part of the Evanson family farm) in McKenzie County, North Dakota, east of Arnegard and west of Watford City.

title: 1985 Dodge Ram Pick-up Truck
description:
7w, 1/35 scale, 100% Lego. Rear axle with spring suspension, trailer coupling. 

Surprisingly I didn't have a proper pick-up truck until now although they are absolutely required on a US-oriented layout. But for a long time I had no idea how to build the sides of the truckbed (what's the correct expression for that btw.?) - quite often they are built out of complete bricks whereas I wanted them to be thinner.

This solution seems to be working though the "bracket-and-tile" (and hinge) building style has its downsides: It's rather difficult to mimic doors and handles, and I haven't found a way to provide some rear-view mirrors yet. 

But well, you can't have everything. In any case this will serve as a standard model on the layout, probably in quite a few variations.

Thanks for looking!

description: Model: Scania R 580 V8 Highline Euro6 6X2 (R-Series 6) VIN: YS2R6X20005418770 1. Registration: 2016-10-31 Company: Kai Andersens Eftf., Verninge, Tommerup (DK) Fleet No.: - Nickname: - License plates: BE50389 (oct. 2016-?) Previous reg.: n/a Later reg.: n/a Retirement age: still active sep. 2020 Photo location: Motorway 501 (Aarhus Syd Motorvejen), Viby J, Aarhus, DK Sometime between autumn 2018 and march 2019, the name on the doors changed to "Birket Autotransport", while the lightbox still said Kai Andersen's Eftf. - this has later changed to Birket Autotransport as well. The truck still (sep. 2020) runs on the same plates, but there have been so-called "registration events" (road tax refunds) in june 2019 and again in may 2020. Going up the steep hill leading sw out of Aarhus past Viby and Stautrup. Underpowered and/or heavily loaded trucks often struggle here. Tip: to locate trucks of particular interest to you, check my collections page, "truck collection" (www.flickr.com/photos/lavulv/collections/72157684190396672/ ) - here you will find all trucks organized in albums, by haulier (with zip-codes), year, brand and country. Retirement age for trucks: many used trucks are offered for sale on international markets. If sold to a foreign buyer, this will not be listed in the danish motor registry, so a "retired" truck may or may not have been exported. In other words, the "retirement age" only shows the age, at which the truck stopped running on danish license plates.
